title: Uncertainty Quantification in Forecast Comparisons
abstract: arXiv:2605.03997v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Skill scores, which measure the relative improvement of a forecasting method over a benchmark via consistent scoring functions and proper scoring rules, are a standard tool in forecast evaluation, yet their sampling uncertainty is rarely rigorously quantified. With modern forecasting applications being increasingly multivariate and involving evaluations across multiple horizons, variables, spatial locations, and forecasting methods, standard tools like the pairwise Diebold-Mariano forecast accuracy test or pointwise confidence intervals fail to account for the multiple comparison problem, leading to inflated Type I error rates and invalid joint inference. To address the lack of a coherent, statistically rigorous framework for quantifying uncertainty across these multi-dimensional evaluation problems, we introduce simultaneous confidence bands for expected scores and skill scores. translated_title: 预测比较中的不确定性量化
translated_abstract: 技能分数通过一致性评分函数和适当评分规则衡量预测方法相对于基准方法的相对改进，是预测评估的标准工具，但其抽样不确定性却很少得到严格的量化。随着现代预测应用日益呈现多元特征，并涉及跨多个预测时域、变量、空间位置和预测方法的评估，诸如成对Diebold-Mariano预测准确性检验或逐点置信区间等标准工具无法处理多重比较问题，导致第一类错误率膨胀和无效的联合推断。为了解决在这些多维评估问题中缺乏连贯且统计上严格的不确定性量化框架这一缺陷，我们提出了针对期望分数和技能分数的同步置信带。我们的框架为联合推断提供了一个通用而灵活的工具……
tldr: 本文针对预测评估中的多重比较问题导致第一类错误率膨胀的缺陷，提出了期望分数和技能分数的同步置信带，为多维预测比较提供了统计上严格的联合不确定性量化框架。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces simultaneous confidence bands for expected scores and skill scores, providing a statistically rigorous framework for joint uncertainty quantification in multi-dimensional forecast comparisons that addresses the multiple comparison problem and inflated Type I error rates.
